tone_statements.citation: Bostoen, Koen. 2009. Shanjo and Fwe as part of Bantu Botatwe: a diachronic phonological approach. In Akinloye Ojo & Lioba Moshi (eds.), Selected Proceedings of the 39th Annual Conference on African Linguistics, 110-130. Somerville, MA: Cascadilla Proceedings Project (www.lingref.com, document #2191).
tone_statements.quote: The high tone anticipation resulting in high prefixes is not observed in Shanjo and Fwe. Whether this high tone anticipation is an innovation distinguishing the eastern BB languages from the western crucially depends on the tonal behaviour of other western BB languages like Totela and Subiya. Even if the tonal notation of Baumbach (1997) is not entirely consistent, it could be indicative that none of the disyllabic noun or verb stems in his work is preceded by a high tone prefix.
tone_statements.locator: p. 123, sec. 3.11 'Diachronic tone shifts' (see also p. 121 on the absence of tone studies for western Botatwe)
tone_statements.summary: Bantu H/L lexical tone assumed (Botatwe); Subiya tone system undescribed as of 2009; only tone-marked source Baumbach 1997 (inconsistent); Baumbach's data show no H-tone noun/verb prefixes (no high tone anticipation).

audit.reasoning: Quote: confirmed verbatim in the now-downloaded Jacottet 1896 djvu text at Grammaire Soubiya p. 5 sect. 7 (record had no page locator; add it). The source also says accented vowels are long (p. 3 sect. 1), consistent with Bantu penultimate prominence, and the parallel Louyi sketch (p. 83 sect. 6) uses the same formula, so nothing internal contradicts the fixed: penultimate syllable coding. But the deciding source is a single 1896 missionary sketch with no tone analysis, no file was held before this compilation, and Glottolog lists no grammar/phonology for Subiya; the two later sketches (Baumbach 1997, 145 pp with tone marking; Ndana et al. 2017 CASAS manual, 113 pp) are print-only and unexamined. No JIPA illustration, dissertation or instrumental study of Subiya prosody was found (CrossRef/OpenAlex; Hence 'thin': old second-tier source, no
audit.second_reader_evidence: ). Page header 'GRAMMAIRE SOUBIYA 5' at djvu line 1654, then '6° Accentuation, § 7. — Comme dans presque toutes les langues Bantou, l'accent tonique retombe en Soubiya sur la pénultième. Ex. : mu-kwáme [scanned mu-kwdme], homme; izûba, soleil, etc.' (lines 1656-1660), followed by the clitic-monosyllable and accented-monosyllabic-verb remarks (lines 1662-1669) exactly as the compilers reports. So the record's source text is verbatim and the locator to add is 'Jacottet 1896, vol. 1, Grammaire Soubiya, 1re partie Phonétique

sources.quote: 'Comme dans presque toutes les langues Bantou, l'accent tonique retombe en Soubiya sur la penultieme. Ex. : mu-kwame, homme; izuba, soleil, etc. Les monosyllabes sont soit proclitiques, soit enclitiques ... Quelques verbes monosyllabiques ont cependant l'accent; ainsi : ba i, ils allerent; ba si ... D'autres ne l'ont pas ainsi ba ti'. Sect. 1: vowels 'breves quand elles ne sont pas accentuees; longues quand elles sont accentuees'.
sources.locator: Grammaire Soubiya p. 5, sect. 7 'Accentuation' (djvu the text); also p. 3 sect. 1 (accented vowels long)
